rv.q: As the central characters, Smith and Ismael Garcia (as Yitzhak) are smoldering coals.

It’s a riotously fun time, and Smith in particular—a celebrated writer-director-performer in their own right—works the crowd with devil-may-care insouciance and quick improvisational chops, occasionally dropping in references to institutions of queer Chicago life like Steamworks.
You cannot leave the theatre without feeling that you have been entertained and uplifted.
Happily, Haven Chicago's new production delivers the goods.
In this strong JD Caudill-directed production, Hedwig is played by Tyler Anthony Smith, making their Haven debut (and, I guess, their Haven swan song as well).

cn.t: Critics praise this production of the iconic rock musical as a triumphant final bow for Haven Theatre, with strong performances bringing emotional depth to the raunchy, heartbreaking story of identity and self-discovery.
